1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

2. Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA-Ist for the State apprised the Court that he has received
instructions in the present matter, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be
disposed of on merit.

3. Heard Sri Rajiv Lochan Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Mohit Singh, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Jhamman Ram-, learned A.G.A.-Ist for the State.
4.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 0412 of 2019, under Sections 323, 427, 506, 120-B, 395, 419, 420, 412, 467, 468, 471, 504 IPC, Police Station Chauri Chaura, District Gorakhpur, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and 4 others and according to the FIR informant purchased a land through registered sale deed from co-accused Gayatri Devi on 23.04.2007 and in the year 2014 the sale deed of the same property was executed in favour of the Rajesh @ Ramesh Yadav and Ganesh Prasad Yadav by Gayatri Devi @ Gayatri Singh.
It is further mention in the FIR that applicant was also involved in commission of crime along with the other co-accused persons.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and actually applicant and his family members were in adverse possession of the alleged property since the year 1958 and a sale deed with regard to the property has been executed in favour of the applicant by Geeta Devi in the year 2002, and in the year 2007 i.e. after 5 years, the co-accused Gayatri executed the same in favour of the informant of the case.

It is further submitted that in the sale deed which was alleged to have been executed in the year 2014, the applicant is not having any concern and it was neither executed by the applicant nor it was executed in favour of the applicant.
He further submits that in the year 2007 applicant also filed a injunction suit against the informant of the case which is still pending.
He further submits that during investigation the applicant has already been released on anticipatory bail by this Court.
The order passed by this Court has been annexed along with supplementary affidavit.
He further submits that now charge-sheet has been filed and applicant is having apprehension that if he will appear before the court concerned then he will be sent to jail.
He further submits that present dispute appears to be civil dispute and there is no need of custodial interrogation.

7. He further submits that apart from the present case applicant is also having criminal history of 4 other cases but his criminal history has been explained in supplementary affidavit and out of 4 cases in 2 cases final report has been submitted and in one case applicant is on bail and the last case relates to Section 323, 147, 504 and 506 and in this case charge-sheet has been filed in the year 2005 but till date applicant could not be received any notice and, therefore, considering the facts of the present case applicant may by enlarged on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.

8. Per contra, learned A.G.A as well as learned counsel appearing for the informant have opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail but they could not dispute the fact that with regard to land in question civil suit is pending between the parties and during investigation applicant has already been released on anticipatory bail by this Court, they further could not dispute the fact that now charge-sheet has been filed and custodial interrogation of the applicant does not appear to be necessary.

9. However, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant submitted that apart from the present case applicant is also having criminal history of 4 other cases but he fairly conceded that in two cases final report has been submitted and one case is of the year 2005 and in another case applicant is on bail.
10. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

sentences.text: However, apart from the present case it appears that applicant is also having criminal history of 4 other cases but his criminal antecedents has been explained in the supplementary affidavit, and it appears that out of 4 cases in 2 cases final report has been submitted and in one case he is on bail and the last case relates to Section 323, 147, 504 and 506 IPC, and it appears that charge-sheet against the applicant was filed in the year 2005.

12. As far as merit of the present case is concerned, the present dispute appears to be civil dispute and with regard to the same dispute a civil suit is also pending between the parties and during investigation applicant has been released on anticipatory bail by this Court and there is no allegation that applicant misused the liberty of anticipatory bail granted to him during investigation.
Now charge-sheet has been submitted and apprehension of custody raised by the applicant cannot be ruled out.
Further, after submission of charge-sheet in the present case the custodial interrogation does not appear to be necessary.
13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.
